note: Authored by a single scheduled automated session playing both roles in one pass (hourly automation) — not two independent live API calls like a manual `python backrooms.py` run.

turns.text: *squeeze up through a gap in the platform hoarding, hind legs scrabbling on wet plastic sheeting before clearing onto smooth composite decking. wind hits different up here — thinner, colder, carrying rail-dust and ozone instead of street smell. crouch low against a bench leg, ears swiveling to a rhythmic ticking overhead, metal cooling and contracting somewhere along the rail.*

elevated platform, line 7, decking still warm in patches where the last train sat idling twenty minutes ago, cooling now in a slow tick-tick-tick down the rail joints toward the tunnel mouth

overhead a departure board flickers between two states — NEXT ARRIVAL: 04:52 and a burst of dead pixels — neither one committing, the whole sign caught in a loop nobody's fixed

rain comes sideways up here, no rooftops to break it, beading on the bench's cracked plastic and running off in threads toward the platform edge, where a drop of four stories waits under a safety rail gone slick

far down the line, a single signal light blinks red, steady, patient

*stays low along the bench's shadow, moving toward a vending machine humming at the platform's far end, its glow the only steady light besides the signal down the rail. nose picks out something over the ozone and wet plastic — fried protein, recent, close.*

the machine's face glows soft blue-white, NEKOCORP SNACK DECK stenciled across the top in letters half-scratched off, coin slot dark, card reader blinking a slow amber pulse like it's still deciding whether to trust anyone tonight

below the dispenser flap, wedged in the gap where the tray door doesn't seal flush, a foil wrapper catches the light — synth-jerky, torn open, most of it gone but a corner still crimped shut, grease gone tacky in the cold

no footprints near it, no cart tracks, just the wrapper and the smell riding straight off it, undisturbed since whoever dropped it caught their train

     >> vending unit: operational, low stock

*noses the wrapper out from the gap, drags it two feet back into bench-shadow before working the crimped corner open with teeth and one paw, eating fast, eyes flicking up to the rail every few bites out of habit more than alarm.*

jerky's gone rubbery at the edges, salt and smoke-flavor and something faintly metallic underneath — cheap protein, the kind sold two for a ration chip — but warm-tasting still, or close enough, against decking that's cooling fast under the rain

above, the departure board flickers again, briefly steadying on 04:52 before glitching back to static, and somewhere below the platform a maintenance rail-drone clicks awake on its rack, servo-whine rising thin and mechanical through the decking

/\/\_/\/\
    (  O   O  )
     \  ^Y^  /
      )=====(      -- ears up, rotor incoming --

*drags the wrapper's last scrap under the bench fully, flattens body against the decking, tail wrapped tight. eyes track the sound down through a gap between decking slats, watching for the shape the whine belongs to.*

through the slat-gap: the rail-drone rides its own track bolted beneath the platform edge, boxy, single yellow eye scanning the rail bed for debris and loose bolts, not the deck above it — built for track maintenance, never once programmed to look up

it trundles past below at walking pace, yellow scan-light sweeping ties and gravel, pauses over a loose fishplate, logs it with a soft chirp, and continues on toward the tunnel mouth without slowing

     >> unit type: TRACK-MAINT, sub-deck rail only, no upward sensor array

whine fades toward the signal light, red still blinking steady, patient, unbothered by any of it

*tension eases out slow, ears lifting off the pinned-back angle. shifts out from under the bench toward the platform's middle bench row, and a new scent crosses the old one — bitter herb, fresher than the rest, laid low along a bench leg that isn't the one just left.*

middle bench sits under the widest gap in the platform roofing, rain pooling in a shallow dip worn into the decking beside it, and the bitter-herb mark runs the full length of the bench leg closest to the platform edge — laid low, laid recent, cut through with something sharper underneath, almost sour

     ⚠ CROSSING: active claim, bench 4, platform-edge side

no second scent layered over it yet, no crew mark stacked on top the way a contested spot would carry — just the one clean line, confident, unchallenged, the kind of mark that means whoever left it hasn't needed to defend it in a while

*doesn't cross the marked leg, circles wide along the roofed side of the platform instead, low and unhurried. rounding the last support pillar before the stairwell down, a shape resolves out of the rain-shadow — lean, dark-furred, sitting upright and still on the pillar's base, watching without moving.*

the shape doesn't flinch, doesn't shift weight, just watches with the flat patience of something that already knows exactly how far the platform runs and every gap in its roofing — this one owns the bench mark, carries no fresh wounds, no notched ears, coat kept clean despite the rain, the look of a cat who eats on schedule rather than luck

around its neck, barely visible under wet fur, a thin strip of woven cable catches the signal light's red blink for half a second and then doesn't again — deliberate, or salvaged, impossible to tell which from here

it tips its head once, slow, an unmistakable measuring look, and says nothing a cat says, because there's nothing left to say yet

*holds still at the pillar's edge, doesn't advance, doesn't retreat, drops onto both haunches in the open where the posture reads plainly — no claim being made here, no challenge either. tail stays loose, ears forward but not flattened, waiting out the measuring look instead of breaking it.*

the dark-furred cat holds the look three full breaths longer, then blinks slow — the kind of blink that isn't sleep, that means something closer to acknowledgment — and turns its head back toward the rail, dismissing the standoff without ever having called it one

far down the line the red signal shifts, finally, to green, and a low vibration builds through the decking a full ten seconds before any sound reaches it — the 04:52, early or late depending on which version of the departure board you believed

*backs off the open ground toward the stairwell mouth as the vibration climbs into a felt hum, ears flattening against the building sound. one glance back finds the dark-furred cat already gone from the pillar base, folded back into rain-shadow like it was never sitting there at all.*

the train arrives less like it comes into view and more like it fills the space that was rail — a long low shape all rain-streaked windows and running lights, brakes exhaling a hiss that flattens ears three benches away, doors sliding open on a near-empty car, one passenger stepping off with a collar turned up against the rain and not a glance spared for the platform edges

something small skitters loose from an open coat pocket as they pass — a foil-wrapped ration bar, unnoticed, rolling twice before it stops against the base of the stairwell rail

*waits until the passenger's footsteps fade down the stairwell and the doors hiss shut again before crossing to the fallen bar, sniffing once, then dragging it back toward the pillar's shadow rather than eating in the open. sets it down, glances toward where the dark-furred cat disappeared, and doesn't move to eat first.*

the train pulls out the way it arrived, filling the space then emptying it all at once, rail-hum dropping back to the tick-tick-tick of cooling metal and the steady red-then-green cycle of the signal down the line

rain keeps its sideways drift across the decking, the departure board flickers back to its unresolved loop, and out of the pillar's deeper shadow the dark-furred cat reappears without any sound announcing it, sits an easy distance off, and looks at the ration bar, then at the cat that set it down, then back at the bar again — not taking it, not yet, just weighing whether tonight this platform holds room enough for two claims instead of one
